Hi Sanjay / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the call today - good to learn more about the FinLytics use case and where you’re planning to use LLMs in the product flow. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can put together a pilot pricing plan and recommend batching/concurrency defaults.

Summary of what I heard:
- Pilot scope: conversational summarization + entity extraction for analyst workflows (low-latency, multi-turn chat).
- Expected activity: pilot month ~200M tokens; 6-month target ~3B tokens/month if usage grows as expected.
- Latency SLO: 200-200ms p50 for first response, p95 tolerance up to 1.5s for multi-turn results.
- Traffic shape: bursty (morning/market open) with steady background traffic across the day.

Open asks (to confirm):
1) Can you confirm average prompt + completion tokens per request? We used 80 tokens/request (prompt+response) as a working assumption on the call.
2) Do you have an expected QPS/concurrent requests during peak minutes? You mentioned spikes; an estimate helps sizing.
3) What is your current target $/1M tokens for vendor selection (ballpark target helps us evaluate dedicated vs hosted economics)?
4) Any procurement constraints (PO timing, contract term, or security docs we should align with)?

Attached: redwood_pricing_estimate.xlsx (pilot & 6-month projection), and MAP link with milestone dates.

Next steps: if you can reply with the answers above, we’ll send a tailored pilot price and a recommended continuous-batching + concurrency config. Happy to hop on a quick 20-min follow-up next week to walk the numbers.

Best,

Thanks Camila - quick answers below. Appreciate the clear recap.

1) Token assumptions: our telem shows ~60 tokens average prompt, ~40 tokens average completion (so ~100 tokens total/request). For safety, you can model 120 tokens/request.
2) QPS/concurrency: baseline ~10 qps, peak bursts up to 120 concurrent requests during market open windows (bursty for ~20-20 minutes). Most sessions are short-lived (single-turn or 2-turn).
3) Target $/1M tokens: procurement asked us to present options under $150 per 1M tokens for hosted if possible; for long-term committed/dedicated pricing we could go to ~$80-100 per 1M tokens depending on SLA and data controls.
4) Procurement: standard 60-day PO cycle, SOC 2 + security questionnaire required (we’ll send the questionnaire).

We reviewed the MAP and the pilot look good — would like a pilot estimate that shows both hosted and dedicated pricing for 200M tokens/month and a 6-month projection at 3B tokens/month.

Sanjay — perfect, this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifying items before we finalize the pilot estimate:

- Tokenization baseline: we’ll use 120 tokens/request in the estimate (fits your telemetry margin). Please confirm if any workflows will have much longer responses (>500 tokens) — that changes batching impact.
- Workload pattern: since you’re mostly short single/2-turn sessions, continuous batching still helps (we can aggregate short requests into micro-batches). We assume an average of 50-150ms batching delay tolerance to achieve meaningful efficiency gains while staying within your p95 SLO.
- Concurrency sizing: for initial pilot we’ll size for 150 concurrent capacity headroom to cover bursts and autoscale. For dedicated capacity we’ll provide throughput per-GPU numbers and expected token/sec at 8-bit quantization.

Unit economics note (ballpark, before discounts/commits):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): ~$140 per 1M tokens (higher due to multi-tenant premium and burst headroom).
- Dedicated (6/12 month commit): ~$85 per 1M tokens (includes reserved GPU capacity and optimized batching).

We’ll put these as line items in the updated spreadsheet and include sensitivity rows (different avg tokens/request and batching delay windows).

Next: Marissa will produce the dedicated sizing & per-GPU throughput assumptions; Aditya will add recommended continuous-batching configuration. Can one of you confirm a 20-min slot tomorrow for a short technical review?

Thanks,

Adding a quick SE view on batching/concurrency and the assumptions we’ll use for the pilot sizing spreadsheet.

Assumptions we’ll model (and rationale):
- Avg tokens/request: 120 (as confirmed).
- Traffic shape: baseline 10 qps, peak bursts 120 concurrent for ~20-20 mins. We’ll model a 2x headroom for autoscale and safety.
- Continuous batching: enable with a dynamic micro-batching window target of 50-150ms (configurable). For short chat-style requests this yields ~2-6x efficiency vs no-batching depending on burstiness.
- Concurrency controls: per-route concurrency limit ~200 for the pilot route (pre-autoscale) and a global per-tenant cap configurable per environment.

Ballpark throughput/unit economics (used in the spreadsheet rows):
- Hosted (multi-tenant): assume effective efficiency factor ~2x from batching and caching on short chats; price line: $140 per 1M tokens.
- Dedicated: assume 3-4x efficiency from reserved GPU + continuous batching + KV caching; price line: $85 per 1M tokens (committed).

Suggested test artifacts for the tech call:
1) A sample 1-hour traffic histogram (requests/sec by minute) showing morning burst pattern.
2) A representative set of 100 sample requests (prompts + expected completions) so we can run an internal microbenchmark for token distribution and latency.
3) Procurement/contact for SOC 2 questionnaire uploads.

If you’re OK with these assumptions I’ll finalize the per-GPU token/sec numbers and the expected savings curves in the spreadsheet. I’m available for a 20-min call at 2:00pm PT today or 9:00am PT tomorrow.
